rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in the body; this is a narrative closer lecture, not an interactive demo beat.
All six chunks carry multi-paragraph, self-carrying content; none is a bare wait-state or single context-dependent bullet.

chunk 1 header 'Wrong is how steering gets in' still holds against the reworded line 13 ('Some went off in the wrong passage' reads as a rule misfiring in the wrong place — still a steering-correction beat). chunk 5 header 'You just ran the compound loop' holds against 'same shape, more names' (one loop, two labelings — the header's singular claim, stated more precisely than the retired wording). All other headers match their chunk content unaffected by either edit.

Re-checked all sub-items across all six chunks. Line 13's triple ('Some were overscoped. Some went off in the wrong passage. Some held for one kind of content and broke for another') keeps three distinct concrete failure modes (breadth / placement / content-type) — third leg still carries new content, passes the third-leg test; the word swap ('fired'→'went off') didn't change the category of the middle leg. Line 43's 'same shape, more names' is a flat equivalence claim, not a stated-then-undercut number: nothing is retracted, no hedge word appears, no specific count is asserted and walked back — it reads as a structural claim (eight named stages are a finer cut of the same four-stage shape), independent of the maintainer's decision to keep the printed sequence. No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction anywhere (line 9's 'Not wrong the way a bad draft is wrong... Wrong the way any first version is wrong...' is a single negation-then-assertion contrast, not the banned two-negations-plus-Z shape). No self-grading superlatives. No abstraction-noun stacks. No verb triplets with an empty leg. Line 39's paired fragments ('Over ninety minutes, not a year. On a trivial bug, not a whole training.') are pairs, which the rule explicitly allows ('cut to a pair').

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: The targeted fix at line 13 holds, checked on the rule's own intent rather than assumed clean because the named term is gone. 'went off' is not in rule 8's list and is not maintainer dialect under any reading: it never appears anywhere in check_*.md or content-rules.md as a term of art (grepped, zero hits), and it resolves via the ordinary English idiom for something triggering/misapplying (an alarm going off, a trap going off) — no knowledge of this repo's 'fires' vocabulary is needed to parse 'went off' as 'activated/applied.' 'passage' is even more clearly plain: this repo's own eval-judge files use 'passage' dozens of times in exactly the dictionary sense ('quote passages', 'per-passage verdicts') — it is not part of any internal taxonomy (unlike 'surface', which content-rules.md itself uses as a jargon organizing noun) and makes no claim on insider knowledge. Both hold as a clean fix. BUT re-running the rule across the whole chunk (not just the edited sentence) surfaces an UNFLAGGED violation the two prior fix cycles missed: chunk 1, line 11, one of the three quoted rule-exhibits reads *"Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go."* — 'forcing function' is named verbatim in rule 8's own illustrative list, immediately beside 'firing' and 'compendium' (the two terms already fixed in this file). Grepped confirmation that this is genuine maintainer dialect, not a term with independent plain-English standing in this repo: every other occurrence of 'forcing function' across curriculum/trainings and curriculum/exercises sits inside maintainer blocks, watch-for tables, or trainer-facing 'per check_pedagogy.md rule 47' rows — never once earned or used in student-facing body prose anywhere in AE101. The maintainer block's own 'Engineer-audience' carve-out on this file names exactly three technical terms cleared for this register — subagent, compendium, plan mode — and pointedly does not include forcing function, which reads as a considered exclusion, not an oversight. Same failure mode the 'fired' fix-cycle named in its own commit message ('I reasoned about what the rule probably covered instead of reading its own examples') — here applied to a location neither fix cycle checked, because both were scoped to the single sentence under repair rather than the whole chunk. The backing block's own claim `corrections-became-rules` treats this quote as a real, verbatim, must-stay-true rule-text exhibit (compendium-rule-quotes source: 'These are quoted as true, so they must stay true'), and its own stated fallback is 'any three real rules spanning pedagogy, formatting and research — the spread is what the beat needs, not these particular three' — so swapping which pedagogy rule gets quoted is a maintainer-sanctioned move, not an invention.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Swap the 'Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go' quote for a different real rule from check_pedagogy.md/check_prompts.md/check_research_claims.md that doesn't carry a banned dialect term — the backing block's own fallback already authorizes this substitution; do not paraphrase 'forcing function' in place, since the backing block requires the quote stay verbatim-true to a real rule.
